detailed_description: Binary to Text converts between 8-bit binary byte groups and readable text in the browser. In Binary to Text mode, paste a sequence such as 01001000 01100101 01101100 01101100 01101111 and press Convert to decode it into text. In Text to Binary mode, type text and the tool converts each character into a padded binary value separated by spaces. The converter ignores spacing in binary input, requires the cleaned binary length to be a multiple of 8, shows an error for invalid byte length, and includes Swap and Copy controls. It is best for simple ASCII-style learning, debugging, and examples rather than file processing, encryption workflows, or complete character-set analysis.
usage_steps: Choose Binary to Text or Text to Binary at the top of the tool.
Paste binary byte groups or type plain text in the input box.
Click Convert and review the result in the output box.
Use Swap to change direction or Copy to copy the current output.
usage_examples: Turn a short classroom example into spaced binary byte groups.
Check whether pasted binary contains a complete set of 8-bit bytes.

faqs.question: What binary format does it expect?
faqs.answer: Use 0 and 1 characters in 8-bit groups. Spaces are fine because the converter removes non-binary separators before decoding.

faqs.question: Why do I see an invalid binary error?
faqs.answer: After spaces and separators are removed, the binary length must divide evenly into 8-bit bytes.

faqs.question: Can I use uploaded files?
faqs.answer: No. It converts typed text and binary strings only; there is no file picker or cipher workflow.

faqs.question: Does Text to Binary support every Unicode character?
faqs.answer: It uses browser character codes and works best for simple text examples. It is not a complete character-set analyzer.
